prompt:
scene_objects: ['Person1', 'Barrier1', 'Charge1', 'DoorPanel1']
task_description: GOTO (to the person to the right of the barrier)

Examples:
Example 1 — spatial word identifies an object (not approach direction):
  task_description: GOTO (to the person behind the couch)
  scene_objects: [DoorPullHandle1, DoorPanel1, Person1, Person2, Charge1, Barrier1, Wall1, Couch1]
  Output: {
    target_object: Person,
    spatial_relation_goto: DEFAULT,
    pov_object_goto: -,
    spatially_related_object: Couch1,
    spatial_relation_obj: BEHIND,
    class_discriminator: CLOSE
  }

Example 2 — spatial word defines approach direction:
  task_description: GOTO (in front of the person)
  scene_objects: [Person1, Person2]
  Output: {
    target_object: Person,
    spatial_relation_goto: FRONT,
    pov_object_goto: -,
    spatially_related_object: -,
    spatial_relation_obj: -,
    class_discriminator: CLOSE
  }

Example 3 — FAR discriminator with approach direction:
  task_description: GOTO (the last person behind the barrier)
  scene_objects: [Person1, Person2, Barrier1]
  Output: {
    target_object: Person,
    spatial_relation_goto: BEHIND,
    pov_object_goto: -,
    spatially_related_object: Barrier1,
    spatial_relation_obj: BEHIND,
    class_discriminator: FAR
  }

Example 4 — single instance, use full ordinal name:
  task_description: GOTO (this person next to the wall)
  scene_objects: [Person1, Wall1]
  Output: {
    target_object: Person1,
    spatial_relation_goto: DEFAULT,
    pov_object_goto: -,
    spatially_related_object: Wall1,
    spatial_relation_obj: NEXT_TO,
    class_discriminator: CLOSE
  }

Example 5 — FAR with no spatial reference object:
  task_description: GOTO (the other person)
  scene_objects: [Person1, Person2, Wall1]
  Output: {
    target_object: Person,
    spatial_relation_goto: DEFAULT,
    pov_object_goto: -,
    spatially_related_object: -,
    spatial_relation_obj: -,
    class_discriminator: FAR
  }

Example 6 — navigate behind a structure (target is the structure itself):
  task_description: GOTO (behind wall)
  scene_objects: [Person1, Wall1, Wall2]
  Output: {
    target_object: Wall,
    spatial_relation_goto: BEHIND,
    pov_object_goto: -,
    spatially_related_object: -,
    spatial_relation_obj: -,
    class_discriminator: CLOSE
  }

Immediate Task: Extract the GOTO navigation parameters from the task_description.

Note: Ask yourself: (1) Is the spatial word identifying an object or defining the approach direction? (2) Are there proximity keywords? (3) Are there multiple instances of the target object?

Output Format:
Return a valid JSON object with exactly these fields:
  target_object         — base name if multiple instances exist; full ordinal (e.g., Cup1) if only one instance.
  spatial_relation_goto — approach direction: BEHIND | FRONT | RIGHT | LEFT | DEFAULT
  pov_object_goto       — point-of-view reference for approach; use '-' if not applicable.
  spatially_related_object — reference object used to identify the target (full ordinal, e.g., Wall1); use '-' if none.
  spatial_relation_obj  — spatial relation for identification: BEHIND | FRONT | RIGHT | LEFT | NEXT_TO | DEFAULT
  class_discriminator   — proximity selection: CLOSE | FAR
